canvas-01.description: The lower part of Sheet 1, below the key map and street index and separated from them by a heavy line, is a 50 foot to an inch map of Franklin Avenue south-east of the Lake Avenue and Mill Street junction. Franklin Avenue runs across the sheet from the bridge over the head race and Church Run on the left towards the right edge, where Sheet 12 continues it. At the upper left stands the Swedesboro Roller Mill and flour mill with a saw mill, wheel house and office, fed by the head race from Lake Narraticon, whose water is drawn at the lower left, with the tail race returning to Church Run. A driveway leads north from Franklin Avenue past the mill. North of the street, block 118 holds a corn crib, a wagon shed, a few dwellings, an auto repair shop and garages; south of it, block 119 holds dwellings and a brick dwelling by the lake. A 4 inch water pipe runs along Franklin Avenue. The sheet's own north arrow points well to the left of the street's modern direction. The upper part of the sheet carries the key map, the legend, notes on the water facilities and fire department, the street and specials index and an inset locating the town in New Jersey; they are not part of this map.
notes: Printed as sheet 1; the canvas also carries the key map, legend and index.
Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street in OpenStreetMap.
Swedesboro Roller Mill (flour mill, capacity 60 barrels) with head race and tail race.
Placed from one hand-picked point (the bend in Franklin Avenue taken as the modern bend at Merkling Street) with assumed scale and rotation; low confidence.

map. Printed sheet 1: key map (600 ft to an inch, not used), key, water and fire notes and street index in the upper part; below a heavy line a 50 ft map of Franklin Av. east of Church Run (Swedesboro Roller Mill, head and tail races, Lake Narraticon), blocks 118 and 119. Configured as one part (canvas-01) masked to the map below the heavy line. No street junction drawn; placed from one hand-picked point (the bend in Franklin Av. taken as the modern bend at Merkling Street) with assumed scale and rotation. The sheet's north arrow disagrees with modern Franklin Street by about 30 degrees; the drawn street was matched to the modern one.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-eastern part of central Swedesboro between Broad Street on the west and Water Street on the east, from 3rd Street and the road along the cemetery wall in the north down to Main Street, with a strip south of Main at the bottom of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Second Street crosses the sheet diagonally, meeting Broad, Church and Water Streets; Ashton runs along the left edge to Main, and Glen Echo Avenue leaves Main at the lower right. The northern blocks hold the W. H. McCullough lumber yard with its lumber sheds, mill work building and lath and shingle piles, a cemetery between Church and Water Streets, and a contractor's storage yard. Most other lots are frame dwellings with outbuildings. South of 2nd Street stand the Swedesboro Public School, an auto repair garage, a plumber and the Y.W.C.A. building; at the corner of Church Street and Main is the Trinity Protestant Episcopal Church with its horse sheds, set in a second large cemetery bounded by a stone wall. Along Main are stores, an auto laundry, a battery and auto repair shop with a bottling house, the Trinity Rectory and the Trinity Protestant Episcopal Parish House. At the lower right Raccoon Creek and the borough limits are drawn, with a coal pile and coal bins by the bridge. Water pipe sizes, hydrants and street widths (50 to 65 feet) are lettered throughout.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
The street lettered only "Road" between Church and Water Streets north of the cemetery is General Harker Lane today.
Trinity Protestant Episcopal Church, rectory and parish house on Main at Church.

map, 50 ft. Broad, Church, Water, 2nd St., Main (Kings Highway), Ashton, Glen Echo Av., 3rd St., Road (General Harker Lane); McCullough lumber yard, public school, Trinity P.E. church, cemetery. Pilot sheet.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the commercial centre of Swedesboro along Main, which runs across the middle of the sheet from Lake Avenue at the left to Ashton at the right. Second Street crosses the top of the sheet, and Railroad Avenue and Allen (Lippincott Av.) run north from Main between blocks of stores, dwellings and small industry; Ashton closes the sheet on the right. South of Main, Mill runs south from Main to Franklin Avenue and the Lake Narraticon mill pond, while Lake Avenue and Park Avenue turn south-west at the lower left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Main runs nearly across the page. Along Main are the Swedesboro Natl. Bank, the Swedesboro Trust Co., the post office, the Swedesboro Opera Ho. and the Swedesboro Hotel, with many stores whose upper floors are dwellings. A large garage with a repair shop, furniture storage and an undertaker's garage occupies the block at the upper right. North of Main stand a feed mill, a hay and feed store, a laundry and carriage and wagon houses. At the bottom, near Franklin Avenue, are the Swedesboro Water Co. pumping station, a garage and repair shop, a needle manufactory and a small mill pond, Lake Narraticon, with Church Run curving across the lower right. Block numbers and the surrounding sheet numbers 2, 4, 6, 7 and 10 are printed at the margins.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap; Mill and Franklin Avenue are Franklin Street today.
Allen, lettered "(Lippincott Av.)", is Allen Street today.
Railroad Avenue is drawn about 8 degrees from the modern line; only its junction with Main was used as control.

map, 50 ft. Downtown Main (Kings Highway) from Lake Av. to Ashton; 2nd St. at top; Railroad Av., Allen (Lippincott Av.), Mill (Franklin Street), Lake Av., Park Av., Grant Av.; Church Run, Lake Narraticon (Mill Pond); national bank, trust co., opera house, hotel, garage. Railroad Av. drawn about 8 degrees off its modern line.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies south-east of the centre of Swedesboro and covers the eastern end of Main and the streets leading to Lake Narraticon. Main crosses the top of the sheet, with Poplar Street meeting it from the north at the upper left and Lake Avenue running down the right-hand edge. East Avenue runs south from Main along the left side of the sheet, Thomson crosses between East Avenue and Park Avenue, and Park Avenue runs south-west from the upper right towards the bottom of the sheet, with a regular row of dwellings on each side. Lake Narraticon fills the lower right corner, its shoreline drawn as a curved line. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 45 degrees to the page. The blocks along Main hold frame dwellings with outbuildings, the Presbyn Church with its horse shed, and the poultry and dressing rooms of J. Clark Helms. At the upper right is the Borough Hall and Fire Dept. 1st, with a fire tower, an auto service station and a wagon shed. Much of the interior of block 101 and the land between Thomson and Park Avenue is blank, as are the lots along the lake. Water pipe sizes, hydrants and street widths of 33 to 66 feet are lettered on the streets. Blocks 8, 9, 11, 52, 53 and 101 are numbered, and sheets 3, 8 and 9 adjoin.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Thomson is Thompson Avenue today.
Placed from four control points (three detected, Park Avenue / Thompson Avenue hand-picked); medium-low confidence.

map, 50 ft. East end of Main (Kings Highway); Poplar St., East Av., Thomson (Thompson Avenue), Park Av., Lake Av.; Borough Hall and fire department; Lake Narraticon. Broken line work (ink 100). Placed from 4 points (3 detected, Park/Thompson hand-picked); the drawn Lake Av. / Park Av. junction lies off the sheet's right edge, so the bend in Lake Av. was not used.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the northern edge of Swedesboro between West Broad Street and Raccoon Creek, north of 3rd Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Raccoon Creek, with the borough limits running along it, curves across the upper half of the sheet, which is otherwise largely blank open ground (blocks 151 and 154). Along West Broad Street on the left edge are frame dwellings, and behind them the large Swedesboro Supply Co. warehouse complex (warehouses No. 1 to No. 8) between Glass Street and Church Street, with oil tanks to the north. Glass Street runs diagonally from Broad Street toward the warehouses. Church Street continues north of the railroad past a group of coloured dwellings. The West Jersey and Seashore Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad crosses the lower part of the sheet from south-west to north-east, with sidings and a railroad section house. South of the tracks the E. F. Hurff canning, preserving and seed works fills the block east of Church Street: pumpkin cooking and storage rooms, grinding and chipping rooms, a warehouse, drying and feed grinding rooms, a repair shop, a boiler house with iron stacks, coal bins and a conveyor, and a water tank and pump house fed from the creek. A cement block manufacturing building stands near Water Street. Along the bottom edge 3rd Street runs from Broad Street past Church Street to Water Street, with a cemetery south of it. Only that bottom row and the two railroad crossings could be matched to modern streets.
notes: Glass Street is not in OpenStreetMap today.
The West Jersey and Seashore Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad is the Salem Running Track in OpenStreetMap.
E. F. Hurff canning, preserving and seeds works and Swedesboro Supply Co. warehouses.

map, 50 ft. W. Broad, Glass St., Church St., 3rd St., Water St., W.J.&S.S. Divn P.R.R.; Swedesboro Supply Co., E. F. Hurff canning, Raccoon Creek. Control only along the bottom (3rd St.) and two rail crossings; upper half extrapolated.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the north-western side of Swedesboro, from the dwellings on Guest, Vanneman, Helms and Weatherby Avenues at the top down across the railroad yard to the blocks around Railroad Avenue, Allen and 2nd Street at the bottom. W. Broad closes the sheet on the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the avenues of the upper half run from upper left to lower right. In the upper half are frame dwellings on lots between Guest Avenue, marked not open, and Weatherby Avenue, with S. B. Patterson's produce warehouse and the Swedesboro Supply Co. basket and crate factory beside the tracks. The middle of the sheet is the Pennsylvania Railroad yard, a broad fan of tracks crossing the sheet from lower left to upper right, with the passenger depot and its platform at Depot Pl., a tower and water pipes. Below the tracks are the Swedesboro Supply Co. lumber and farm implement sheds, Stokes, Horner's warehouse for boxes, crates and sweet potatoes, and dwellings along Railroad Avenue, Colon Street and Allen. At the right are St. Joseph's R.C. Church with its rectory, parish house, horse shed and poultry house, and a row of dwellings along Broad. Pipe sizes, street widths of 50 to 60 feet and block numbers 111 to 114, 153, 166, 15 and 6 are lettered. The adjoining sheets 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 are noted at the margins.
notes: Depot Pl. is the line of 3rd Street in OpenStreetMap west of Allen; 3rd Street is drawn along the south side of the tracks to the right.
Guest Avenue is marked "not open" on the sheet.
Colon Street and Glass Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Allen Street and Vanneman Avenue and Broad Street and Vanneman Avenue meet in OpenStreetMap beyond where the sheet draws them; those junctions were excluded.

map, 50 ft. Guest (not open), Vanneman, Helms, Weatherby, Leahy Avs.; P.R.R. tracks and passenger depot, Depot Pl. (3rd Street in OpenStreetMap), 3rd St., Railroad Av., Colon St., Allen, 2nd St., Broad and W. Broad, Glass St.; St. Joseph's R.C. church, Swedesboro Supply Co., S. B. Patterson produce warehouse.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the railroad corner of central Swedesboro. The Pennsylvania Railroad yard (W.J. & S.S. R.R.) crosses the upper half of the sheet from lower left to upper right, with Depot Pl. along its south side, and 2nd St. runs across the middle from Richardson Avenue at the left to Railroad Avenue at the right. Grant Avenue runs diagonally through the middle blocks, Richardson Avenue runs down the left side, and Auburn Avenue and Main cross the bottom. Helms Avenue appears at the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 40 degrees to the page. In the upper half are the produce trade buildings beside the tracks: Franklin Black's commission merchant warehouse, W. H. Longacre's fruit and produce warehouse, E. H. Black's fruit and produce warehouse (marked fire ruins), a long produce shipping shed, a freight depot and a small storage shed. H. K. Shoemaker's farm implements and warehouse stands at the left by the tracks, with the Union A.M.E. Church south of it. Along 2nd Street and Grant Avenue are dwellings, stores and a cemetery at the right; at the bottom are an auto repair garage, a garage with a capacity of 15 cars and the M.E. Church. Pipe sizes, street widths of 33 to 50 feet and block numbers 8, 9, 12, 13 and 153 are lettered, and sheets 3, 6 and 8 adjoin.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Grant Avenue and its junction with 2nd Street were not detected; the sheet is placed from five points on Richardson, 2nd Street, Railroad Avenue and Main.

map, 50 ft. P.R.R. yard and freight depot, Depot Pl., 2nd St., Richardson, Grant, Railroad and Auburn Avs., Main, Helms Av.; produce warehouses (Franklin Black, W. H. Longacre, E. H. Black), H. K. Shoemaker, Union A.M.E. and M.E. churches, cemetery.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the south-western edge of central Swedesboro, between the railroad at the top and Main at the bottom. 2nd St. crosses the middle of the sheet from the left edge to Richardson Av. at the right, where it meets Richardson near the railroad; Auburn Av. runs from the middle left to the lower right, and Poplar and East Av. run down to Main at the bottom. Locke Av. is drawn at the upper left, with the borough limits marked beside it. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 55 degrees to the page. In the upper half the Swedesboro Ice and Cold Stge Co. stands at the left, with its engine room, freezing vats, cold storage warehouse and shipping room, beside the W. J. & S. S. Div'n P.R.R. (Salem Branch). Beside the tracks at the right is the large Wm. W. Dilks and Son Inc. basket factory, with warehouses, packing, cutting and sorting rooms, a crate storage building and a steam room. South of the tracks are the Swedesboro Supply Co. basket warehouse, and B. P. Lawrence's lumber and coal yard with lumber sheds, coal bins and a brick shed. The middle is largely blank. At the bottom, along Main, are rows of dwellings, a greenhouse, a garage, and Fords Hotel at the lower right. Block numbers 14, 50, 51, 115 and 7 to 9 are lettered, as are street widths of 33 to 40 feet.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Locke Avenue is drawn running north-east here, at a different bearing from the modern Locke Avenue line; it was not used as control.
Auburn Avenue and Kings Highway meet 92 ft beyond the sheet edge, so that junction is not used.

map, 50 ft, turned about 57 degrees. Locke Av., 2nd St., Richardson, Auburn Av., Poplar, East Av., Main; Swedesboro Ice & Cold Storage Co., Wm. W. Dilks & Son basket factory, B. P. Lawrence lumber and coal, Fords Hotel. Locke Av. not used as control (drawn at another bearing).

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 9 is the main map: the south-western part of Swedesboro along Main Street (Kings Highway) between East Avenue at the top of the sheet and the block south of Mechanic Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Main Street runs down the right half of the sheet, with frame dwellings, a few stores and an auto repair garage on both sides; Chestnut Street, drawn only 18 feet wide, leaves it to the east. Auburn Avenue runs diagonally up the left side of the sheet, with the First Baptist Church (Coloured), a concrete block building, at the corner of Locke Avenue. Locke Avenue enters from the left edge, where the A-B match line marks its continuation in the inset at the top left. Mechanic Street runs from Auburn Avenue east to Main Street near the bottom, lined with dwellings, auto repair and storage buildings and a repairing shop. Block 51 between Auburn Avenue and Main Street is largely open land in long lots, and block 162 west of Auburn Avenue is blank. Blocks 52 and 161 lie east of Main. The scale bar, water pipe sizes (6 and 8 inch on Main) and street widths (67 feet on Main, 33 on Locke) are lettered.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Chestnut Street is drawn 18 feet wide.
First Baptist Church (Coloured) on Auburn Avenue at Locke Avenue.

map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Main, East Av., Chestnut St., Auburn Av., Mechanic, Locke Av.); part 2 inset at top left (Locke Av. west of match line A-B, by the railroad and oil tanks), drawn at the same scale and rotation and carried from part 1 through the A-B match line.

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 9 is a small inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, framed by a heavy line. It continues Locke Avenue north-west of the A-B match line drawn on the main map, at the same scale (50 feet to an inch) and the same rotation, north toward the upper left. Locke Avenue, 33 feet wide, crosses the inset diagonally; 2nd Street is lettered at the top left corner where it meets Locke Avenue. South-west of Locke Avenue, in block 162, stand an office and a pair of automobile garages with oil and gasoline tanks, and along the left edge the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Division of the Pennsylvania Railroad run past with the borough limits beside them. North-east of Locke Avenue is block 115. The inset holds no complete street junction of its own and was placed from the two edges of Locke Avenue where they cross the A-B match line, carried from the main map.
notes: Placed through the A-B match line from part 1 of the sheet; low confidence.
Oil and gasoline tanks by the railroad in block 162.

map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Main, East Av., Chestnut St., Auburn Av., Mechanic, Locke Av.); part 2 inset at top left (Locke Av. west of match line A-B, by the railroad and oil tanks), drawn at the same scale and rotation and carried from part 1 through the A-B match line.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the southern end of Main in Swedesboro, with Main running down the right-hand side of the sheet. Bridgeport Av. crosses from the left edge to Main in the upper half, Turner Av. meets Main in the lower half, and South runs along the bottom edge. Blue-Bell Pl. runs north and south through the left half. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 27 degrees to the page. At the top is the Swedesboro High School, a large building with a gymnasium and auditorium, set in an Athletic Field, with the compass at the upper left. West of Main are frame dwellings along Bridgeport Av. and Turner Av., a manufacturing farm implements and blacksmith shop on Main, and blocks 102 and 103 with scattered outbuildings. East of Main the lots run back as a long row of dwellings, stores and outbuildings, with a poultry house, wagon shed, manure shed and, near the bottom, a brooder house. Several large areas of the left half are blank. Block numbers 54, 102, 103, 115, 116, 161 and 163 are lettered, and Main is marked as 66 feet wide with 4 and 6 inch water pipes along it.
notes: Main is Kings Highway in OpenStreetMap.
Blue-Bell Place is drawn on the line of Mayhew Avenue in OpenStreetMap; two junctions on Mayhew fitted to 1 m.
South is South Avenue today; it is lettered without a suffix.
map, 50 ft. Main (Kings Highway) south of Mechanic, Bridgeport Av., Turner Av., South, Blue-Bell Place (on the line of Mayhew Avenue); Swedesboro High School, athletic field.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 11 is the main map: the north-western residential district of Swedesboro between Leahy Avenue and West Broad Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. West Broad Street runs diagonally across the upper right of the sheet and turns south along the right edge; Raccoon Creek and the borough limits follow it on the north-east, with a row of narrow dwelling lots and a poultry house between the street and the creek. Leahy Avenue runs from the lower left up to West Broad Street; Anderson Avenue and Weatherby Avenue cross it towards the south-east, and Helms Avenue runs north-east to West Broad Street near the lower right corner. Most lots hold frame dwellings with garages and sheds; a chapel and school of the Seventh Day Adventists stand on the large block 105. Blocks 104, 106, 108, 109, 110 and 111 are numbered, block 108 largely empty. Vanneman Avenue is lettered at the very bottom left corner. The upper left of the sheet is an inset behind a heavy line and is described separately.
notes: West Broad is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Seventh Day Adventists chapel and school on block 105.
Fow Avenue in OpenStreetMap crosses blocks 105 and 108, where the sheet draws no street.

map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Leahy, Anderson, Weatherby, Helms Avs., W. Broad; 7th Day Adventists school); part 2 inset at top left behind a heavy line (Locke, Weatherby, Vanneman, Guest (not opened) and Leahy Avs.), Locke Av. drawn in faint lines.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 11 is an inset in the upper left of the sheet, bounded below and on the right by a heavy line. It shows the blocks north-west of the main map, between Locke Avenue and Leahy Avenue, at the same scale (50 feet to an inch) and rotation, north toward the upper right. Locke Avenue runs along the upper left, drawn in faint lines, with the borough limits just beyond it. Weatherby Avenue, Vanneman Avenue and Guest Avenue run from Locke Avenue towards the south-east; Guest Avenue is marked as not opened. A short piece of Leahy Avenue is drawn at the lower right corner of the inset. Blocks 109, 110, 152 and 153 hold a scattering of frame dwellings and garages, with much open land. Street widths of 50 feet are lettered on each street.
notes: Guest Avenue is marked "not opened".
Locke Avenue is drawn in faint lines; the Leahy Avenue / Vanneman Avenue corner was hand-picked.

map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Leahy, Anderson, Weatherby, Helms Avs., W. Broad; 7th Day Adventists school); part 2 inset at top left behind a heavy line (Locke, Weatherby, Vanneman, Guest (not opened) and Leahy Avs.), Locke Av. drawn in faint lines.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 12 is the main map: the north-eastern entrance to Swedesboro along North Main Street east of Raccoon Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. North Main Street runs across the bottom of the sheet from the iron bridge with plank floor over Raccoon Creek on the left, where the borough limits cross, to the right edge. Paulsboro Road leaves it near the middle and runs north-north-east to the top of the sheet, lined on both sides by frame dwellings with numbered lots. On the right is the Otto C. Rode poultry and eggs establishment with coops, an office and shipping building and a wagon shed. Near the creek the Geo. A. Rode coal, ice and fertilizer yard has a fertilizer house, an office with scales and other buildings; a store, an auto repair shop and dwellings face North Main Street. The branch of Raccoon Creek runs along the bottom edge south of North Main Street. Much of the sheet (blocks 158, 159, 160) is open land. The upper left of the sheet is an inset behind a heavy line and is described separately.
notes: North Main is Kings Highway and Paulsboro Road is Swedesboro Paulsboro Road in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 12 is an inset in the upper left of the sheet, framed by a heavy line, continuing Franklin Avenue south-east of the strip drawn on Sheet 1. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with Franklin Avenue running down the inset and its own north arrow. Block 118 lies east of the street and block 119 west of it; a few frame dwellings, coops, a storage building and a wagon shed stand on the large lots, and much of both blocks is empty. A 4 inch water pipe and a hydrant are drawn along Franklin Avenue, which is lettered 50 feet wide. The edges of the inset are marked no exposure. No street joins Franklin Avenue within the inset.
notes: Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street in OpenStreetMap.
